idh.reasoning: For IDH status considered independently, the imaging pattern leans toward IDH-wildtype because age_years is in a middle-aged adult range, the tumor has a large Whole Tumor Volume (mL), very large ED Volume (mL) and high Proportion of Oedema, plus substantial NCR Volume (mL) and reported Proportion Necrosis, which are more typical of aggressive IDH-wildtype diffuse glioma than lower-grade IDH-mutant glioma. T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present is absent, which argues against the classic IDH-mutant astrocytoma mismatch pattern, although this is not definitive. Against IDH-wildtype, Enhancement Quality is only mild, ET Volume (mL) and Proportion Enhancing are very small, Cortical involvement is present, Deep WM invasion is absent, and midline_shift_present is absent; these features can be seen with IDH-mutant tumors and reduce certainty. Overall, the aggressive edema/necrosis burden outweighs the mild enhancement and cortical features, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.

Because the location and edema/necrosis pattern are less typical for 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma, the best estimate is non-codeleted.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on conventional MRI metadata without DWI/ADC, perfusion, spectroscopy, SWI/GRE, or calcification assessment. The very small enhancing volume and mild enhancement introduce uncertainty, but the large edema burden and reported necrotic/non-enhancing core favor an aggressive IDH-wildtype, non-codeleted grade 4 phenotype. Tissue diagnosis and molecular testing remain required.
